source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Pigs need six kinds of nutrients. Protein (from fish, snails, tofu waste, peanuts, high-protein pasture, or fodder-tree leaves) builds muscle and supports reproduction — pigs grow faster when some animal protein is included because animal sources supply two key amino acids, lysine and methionine, that plant protein lacks in sufficient amounts. Carbohydrate (from corn, rice bran, cassava, sweet potato, taro) is the main energy source; too much makes pigs fat. Fat (from coconut or palm oil) supports growth, milk production, and fertility. Vitamins (from plant oils and green leaves) support health and metabolism. Minerals (from fish, bone meal, snail shells, limestone soil, banana stem) support bone growth and digestion. Water makes up over 70% of a pig's body — pigs denied water for 24–48 hours can develop salt poisoning and die, so clean water must always be available; never use irrigation, roadside, or stagnant water.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
